variables.meaning: the flow rate, the volume of fluid that passes a location through an area during a period of time
the volume of fluid that passes the location in the elapsed time
the elapsed time over which the volume passes the location
the cross-sectional area of the river, pipe or other conduit the fluid flows through
the average velocity of the fluid across that area, which the text refers to after this as the speed
the cross-sectional area of the tube at point 1
the cross-sectional area of the tube at point 2, which is smaller where the tube narrows
the average speed of the fluid at point 1
the average speed of the fluid at point 2, which must be greater for the same volume to pass in the same time
the flow rate past point 1
the flow rate past point 2, which equals the flow rate past point 1 because the fluid is incompressible
the number of branches the tube has at point 1
the number of branches at point 2, such as the capillaries an artery divides into
the radius of the hose, the nozzle or the vessel, which the cross-sectional area is computed from
the absolute pressure in the fluid, which is the first term of Bernoulli’s equation
the density of the fluid, which Bernoulli’s equation takes to be the same at every point
the velocity of the fluid at the point
the height of the point above some reference point
the acceleration due to gravity, which gives the fluid the weight the third term accounts for
the pressure at point 1 along the path the bit of fluid follows
the pressure at point 2 along the same path
the speed of the fluid at point 1
the speed of the fluid at point 2
the height of point 1 above the reference point
the height of point 2 above the reference point, which is often chosen to be zero
the kinetic energy of a volume of fluid, which divided by that volume is the second term of Bernoulli’s equation
the gravitational potential energy of a volume of fluid, which divided by that volume is the third term
the volume of the bit of fluid each energy is divided by
the net work done on the fluid to push it into a narrower channel, which is where the increased kinetic energy comes from
the mass of the bit of fluid, which the density replaces when each term is taken per unit volume
the pressure at the first point, which for Torricelli’s theorem is the surface of the reservoir
the pressure at the second point, which for Torricelli’s theorem is the outlet, where the emerging water is surrounded by the atmosphere
the speed of the fluid at the first point
the speed of the fluid at the second point
the height of the first point
the height of the second point
the height the water drops, the difference between the two heights
the density of the fluid, which cancels out of Torricelli’s theorem because the fluid is incompressible
the acceleration due to gravity
the flow rate, which multiplies each term of Bernoulli’s equation to turn an energy per unit volume into a power
the pressure a pump supplies to the fluid, so that the product of pressure and flow rate is the power the pump supplies
the coefficient of viscosity, the friction within a fluid, which is greater the greater the force needed to shear the fluid
the force required to keep the top plate moving at a constant velocity against the fluid’s viscosity
the speed of the top plate, and of the layer of fluid in contact with it
the area of the plate in contact with the fluid
the distance between the two plates, across which the speed of the fluid falls from that of the top plate to zero
the flow rate through the tube, which is in the direction from high to low pressure
the pressure at the low-pressure end of the tube
the pressure at the high-pressure end of the tube
the resistance to flow, which includes everything except pressure that affects the flow rate
the length of the tube, which the resistance is directly proportional to
the radius of the tube, which the resistance depends on through the fourth power, so that a small change in it has a very large effect
the Reynolds number for flow in a tube, a unitless quantity that reveals whether the flow is laminar or turbulent
the density of the fluid
the speed of the fluid in the tube
the radius of the tube
the viscosity of the fluid, which the Reynolds number is inversely proportional to
the Reynolds number for an object moving in a fluid, which indicates whether the flow around the object is laminar or turbulent
the density of the fluid the object moves through
the object’s speed in the fluid
a characteristic length of the object, a sphere’s diameter for example
the viscosity of the fluid
the viscous drag, the resistance force the fluid’s viscosity exerts on the moving object, which grows with speed
the drag force on a small sphere moving slowly in a fluid, given by Stokes’ law
the radius of the small sphere Stokes’ law applies to
the buoyant force on the falling object, which depends on the density of the object relative to the fluid
the weight of the object falling through the fluid
the terminal speed, the constant speed a falling object reaches once the drag and the buoyant force balance its weight and its acceleration becomes zero
the root-mean-square distance, the statistical average of the distance a molecule travels by diffusion in a given time
the diffusion constant for the particular molecule in a specific medium, which gets progressively smaller for more massive molecules
the time the molecule has had to diffuse

glossary.definition: the physics of fluids in motion
abbreviated Q, it is the volume V that flows past a particular point during a time t, or Q = V/t
a unit of volume, equal to 10⁻³ m³
the equation resulting from applying conservation of energy to an incompressible frictionless fluid: P + 1/2ρv² + ρgh = constant, through the fluid
Bernoulli’s equation applied at constant depth: P₁ + 1/2ρv₁² = P₂ + 1/2ρv₂²
a type of fluid flow in which layers do not mix
fluid flow in which layers mix together via eddies and swirls
the friction in a fluid, defined in terms of the friction between layers
the resistance to laminar flow of an incompressible fluid in a tube: R = 8ηl/πr⁴
the rate of laminar flow of an incompressible fluid in a tube: Q = (P₂ − P₁)πr⁴/8ηl
a dimensionless parameter that can reveal whether a particular flow is laminar or turbulent
a resistance force exerted on a moving object, with a nontrivial dependence on velocity
the speed at which the viscous drag of an object falling in a viscous fluid is equal to the other forces acting on the object (such as gravity), so that the acceleration of the object is zero
the movement of substances due to random thermal molecular motion
a type of membrane that allows only certain small molecules to pass through
the transport of water through a semipermeable membrane from a region of high concentration to one of low concentration
the transport of any molecule other than water through a semipermeable membrane from a region of high concentration to one of low concentration
the back pressure which stops the osmotic process if neither solution is pure water
the back pressure which stops the osmotic process if one solution is pure water
the process that occurs when back pressure is sufficient to reverse the normal direction of osmosis through membranes
the process that occurs when back pressure is sufficient to reverse the normal direction of dialysis through membranes
the process in which a living membrane expends energy to move substances across
